subtopics.title: Link-Layer Addressing and ARP
subtopics.summary: Link-layer (MAC) addresses and how they differ from network-layer IP addresses; the ARP protocol for resolving IP-to-MAC addresses; sending datagrams to nodes off the local subnet.

subtopics.title: Ethernet: Frame Format and Evolution
subtopics.summary: The structure of the Ethernet frame (data field, source/destination addresses, type field, CRC) and Ethernet's history and enduring dominance as the standard LAN technology.

subtopics.title: Switch Forwarding, Filtering, and Self-Learning
subtopics.summary: How a switch uses its switch table to forward or filter incoming frames based on destination MAC addresses, and how it builds and ages table entries automatically via self-learning, making it a transparent plug-and-play device.

subtopics.title: Properties of Link-Layer Switching
subtopics.summary: Advantages of switches over broadcast links and hubs: eliminating collisions through dedicated per-host bandwidth, full-duplex send/receive on each interface, and simplified network administration.

subtopics.title: Switches versus Routers
subtopics.summary: Comparing link-layer switches (implementing layers 1-2, forwarding on MAC addresses) with routers (implementing layers 1-3, forwarding on IP addresses), and the trade-offs in choosing between them.

subtopics.title: Virtual LANs (VLANs)
subtopics.summary: How multiple virtual LANs can be created over a single physical LAN/switch infrastructure, providing traffic isolation and flexible VLAN membership.
